purpose:
This policy says how {{HOSPITAL_NAME}} meets NABH Hospitals 6th Edition standard COP.19: Nutritional therapy is provided to patients consistently and collaboratively.

It covers objective elements COP.19.a–e (5 elements).

This policy owns COP.19. Related AAC, PRE, IPC/HIC, HRM and MOM duties stay with those policies — cross-reference only.

Words marked «like this» are defaults. A blank marked «________» must be filled before issue.
scope:
This policy applies to staff who deliver or oversee the care described in COP.19 at {{HOSPITAL_NAME}}, including the «Dietetics In-Charge», treating doctors, nurses and the Quality Coordinator.

It covers 5 objective elements (COP.19.a, COP.19.b, COP.19.c, COP.19.d, COP.19.e).

Boundaries: do not copy SHCO COP wording. Do not overwrite AAC policies. Spell out abbreviations on first use in training materials.
policy_statement:
{{HOSPITAL_NAME}} implements COP.19 so that nutritional therapy is provided to patients consistently and collaboratively..

Staff follow written guidance, keep the records listed in the OE table, and escalate when stop-work triggers fire (if this policy includes a stop-work section).
procedure_steps:
5.1 Patients admitted to the organisation are screened for nutritional risk

Patients admitted to the organisation are screened for nutritional risk.

Method note (from guidebook interpretation): Nutritional screening is done by the caregiver (doctor or nurse).

5.2 Nutritional assessment is done for patients found at risk during nutr..

Nutritional assessment is done for patients found at risk during nutritional screening.

Staff follow the written guidance and record the action in the medical record or the department register named for this element.

5.3 The therapeutic diet is planned and provided collaboratively

The therapeutic diet is planned and provided collaboratively.

Staff follow the written guidance and record the action in the medical record or the department register named for this element.

5.4 Patients receive food according to the written order for the diet

Patients receive food according to the written order for the diet.

Staff follow the written guidance and record the action in the medical record or the department register named for this element.

5.5 When families provide food, they are educated about the patient’s die..

When families provide food, they are educated about the patient’s diet limitations.

Staff follow the written guidance and record the action in the medical record or the department register named for this element.
responsibility:
Medical Superintendent
- Accountable that COP.19 is resourced and followed.

Dietetics In-Charge
- Owns day-to-day implementation and records for this standard.

Treating doctors / nurses / technicians (as applicable)
- Deliver care as written; escalate stop-work triggers without delay.

Quality Coordinator
- Audits this policy «quarterly»; holds training acknowledgements.

definitions: Nutritional therapy is provided to patients consistently and collaboratively.
exceptions:
1. Do not skip: Patients admitted to the organisation are screened for nutritional risk.
2. Do not skip: Nutritional assessment is done for patients found at risk during nutritional screening.
3. Do not skip: The therapeutic diet is planned and provided collaboratively.
4. Do not skip: Patients receive food according to the written order for the diet.
5. Do not skip: When families provide food, they are educated about the patient’s diet limitations.
6. Staff who see a COP.19 rule broken report it the same shift to the «department in-charge» or the «Medical Superintendent».
monitoring_audit:
The Quality Coordinator audits this policy «quarterly».

What is monitored each quarter:

- Sample of records for each OE COP.19.a–e.
- Asterisked elements (a) have document evidence as required.
- CORE elements (none) show no critical gaps in the sample.
- Stop-work events (if any) are logged with outcome.

This policy is reviewed «annually», and sooner after a related adverse event.
training_competency:
Staff covered by this policy are trained at induction and «once a year» after that. Training covers the What-we-do steps, non-negotiables and stop-work (if present).
